project_fields.name: INDUX — Industrial Telemetry Monitoring & Incident Intelligence
project_fields.short_description: Local-first industrial monitoring with telemetry dashboards, incident triage, and Gemma-powered equipment assessments.
project_fields.description:
INDUX is a local-first industrial telemetry monitoring and incident intelligence prototype for viewing equipment, sensor readings, anomalies, and subsystem health.

The React and TypeScript operations interface provides an asset inventory, historical telemetry charts, an incident queue with acknowledgement and resolution workflows, system health views, and a telemetry ingestion simulator. It supports a live backend connection and a built-in demo simulation mode.

The Python FastAPI backend stores telemetry and incidents in SQLite, validates incoming readings, applies configurable demo thresholds, groups repeated anomalies into incidents, and exposes REST endpoints and WebSocket invalidations. Monitoring does not issue equipment-control commands.

A separate FastAPI AI service checks supplied sensor readings against configured limits and calls the local Ollama API with Gemma 3 (gemma3:4b by default, configurable through GEMMA_MODEL) to generate a concise equipment assessment from the anomalies and limitations. It falls back to a predefined explanation when the model is unavailable. The backend MVP currently keeps its LLM integration disabled; the AI service is a separate component rather than an integrated end-to-end backend feature.

The frontend and AI service include MIT licenses. This is a localhost-oriented prototype with illustrative thresholds and simulated demo data, not a production industrial control or safety system.
